{{Short description|Chaotic 2D map related to the Bogdanov–Takens bifurcation}}
[[File:Bogdanov map.png|thumb|300px|Example with ε=0, k=1.2, μ=0.]]
In [[dynamical systems theory]], the '''Bogdanov map''' is a [[chaos theory|chaotic]] 2D [[map (mathematics)|map]] related to the [[Bogdanov–Takens bifurcation]]. It is given by the transformation:

:<math>
\begin{cases}
x_{n+1} = x_n + y_{n+1}\\
y_{n+1} = y_n + \epsilon y_n + k x_n (x_n - 1) + \mu x_n y_n
\end{cases}
</math>

The Bogdanov map is named after [[Rifkat Bogdanov]].
